parts.text:
From Source 1, identify the number of people in the world who do not have access to
electricity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: From Source 2, identify two reasons for increasing the production of electricity.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which reason for increasing the production of electricity do you think is the most important?
Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why the production of electricity is a global issue.

text: Study Sources 1 and 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘We can generate electricity without harming the environment.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘One person produces about 1.5 kilograms of household waste per day.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Leo’s statement. Explain why this is a prediction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Sophia is arguing that people should adopt a simpler lifestyle and use less electricity.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one fact from Sophia’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this fact supports her argument.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Leo’s or Sophia’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to reduce the impact of electricity production on the environment.
The following actions are being considered:
• Encourage people to live simpler lifestyles that use less electricity.
• Develop cleaner more sustainable ways to produce electricity.
• Increase the price of electricity so that people use less.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
